name: Whole system
ownerWords:
F*UCKING WATCH THIS!QQQQ!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! 

reorganize duties have a 30 minute trigger that checks all this
goal: When nobody works, agent RAM drops: once no session has streamed or run a tool for the quiet window (15 min by default), Settings > Hosts shows Agent sessions under 5 GB. Every minute of the last 30 runs clean too: the boxes stay usable, no start or wake waits over 10 minutes, and no turn waits while slots are free. No tool call sits an hour with no output and no progress. Open steps that nobody moves moved to the Chat system duty on 10-19, so this duty keeps one headline and 3 metrics (c75).

metrics.label: Agent sessions GB on Settings > Hosts once nobody worked for the quiet window
Minutes in the last 30 the system ran clean
Starts or wakes that waited over 10 minutes
Tool calls that wrote nothing for an hour with no progress, or a kernel burning CPU with no output
Playwright or Puppeteer browsers agents run on the Mac

onMiss: Read the detail first. Each missed metric gets one fix job: if its plan step (duty "<dutyId>/<metricKey>") has a live job, message that job with this run's numbers; else start one with await rlm.create_session(brief, name=..., cwd="/Users/sieunpark/Documents/Github/sieun-pi") and set it on the step. Unusable minutes on the harness side and queue holds: the job fixes pi-pool's queue or the chat service's start path with a test and releases, and adds no RAM gate, hold or cap (c88). Unusable minutes on the app or owner side: tell this chat one line with the minutes and the owner, for ops guy. Quiet agent GB: the job reads the quiet_agents and agents_now detail, finds what the agent sessions still hold with nobody working (workers and kernels of sessions in a provider or pool wait, a hung worker, orphan processes), fixes why it was not freed with a test, and releases; a fix inside Prime goes to the chat as a native change (c92, c93). Oversized processes: one line to this chat with the numbers. Hung calls: for each hung_call line, message the chat it names (its chat id is the line's chat) with the session, its minutes and its command, and ask it to interrupt that call (its rlm handle or the session's own kernel) or fix what it waits on; send nothing to stop it yourself. Mac test browsers: for each test_browser line, message the chat it names (its chat id is the line's chat) with the pid and session, and ask it to stop that browser once its current run ends and do that browsing in Aside through the aside-browser skill (c177); a line with no chat names a duty or ssh command, so fix that duty's precheck or tell this chat one line. Never kill a session mid-turn or restart the Prime daemon or :5182. All on target: end with no message.
